originality.rationale: Compared full substantive statements and critical implications, not titles: Sauer gives the Katětov baseline, Csikvári–Lin already know the seven-spider as a graph-homomorphism obstruction, and the published type-polynomial formula for {1,2}-metrics omits the distance-three restrictions. An earlier capped-path/cycle type calculation already supplies the path count (acknowledged and excluded from the claimed novelty), but no compared prior theorem supplies the capped-tree local degree-neighborhood count and the all-order exact path/spider discrepancy. The verdict is a best-knowledge, same-model assessment with explicit residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently phrased literature may already contain the capped-tree counting identity or the same order-seven comparison.
The tree E7 is known in graph homomorphism theory, so any novelty rests on this specific metric-type invariant and exact formulas, not on the tree’s identity.
The theorem does not solve the global minimization problem beyond seven vertices.

The exact path count in the infinite family was previously calculated for capped paths and cycles; novelty is restricted to the all-tree structural formula, sharp first branching failure, and infinite spider-versus-path gap.

value.rationale: The precise first failure of the path-minimum principle is a motivated, sharp boundary for a natural model-theoretic extension count, in contrast with known path-extremal tree homomorphism theorems. The all-order neighbor-degree identity and explicit infinite family E_n give a structural explanation and a nonzero exact discrepancy \(2^{n-5}\) for every n≥8. It does not rely on an arbitrary small graph slice or assert a known E7 shape as newly discovered; it does not overclaim global minimum for higher orders.
